“When the rat approached the cat, the cat took him and held him close,
greeting him and shaking his hand.

When the mongoose saw that-
and the owl too-they left having given up on the rat, retreating disappointed,

p.n: The Rat Begins to Cut the Rope

body.p:
and the rat took to
cutting the cat’s bonds; he cut them little by little.”

p.n: The Cat Deems the Rat's Efforts Slow

body.p:
“When the cat noticed
that the rat was not hard at work cutting the net, he judged him to be slow and said,
‘I don’t see that you are serious in cutting my bond. If, having attained your want, you have changed from
your earlier vow and tarried at my need],

well it is not fit for a noble,
such as yourself], to tarry in fulfilling the need of his companion once he has fulfilled his own need.

p.n: The Cat States the Rat's Duty of Reciprocation

body.p:
You found in my prompt amity benefit and deliverance from perishing,
as you have seen; you owe me reward accordingly

and ought not remember anything
from the times of hostility, for the truce that has transpired between us should
make you forget that, since merit lies in loyalty and treachery begets evil consequences.

The noble person is always grateful, free of grudge,
one good quality makes him forget many harmful qualities.

p.n: The Punishment of Betrayal Comes Swiftly
